title: Refold a Grid Into New Dimensions
statement:
You get a grid grid with m rows and n columns, and two numbers rows and cols. Refold the grid into a new grid of rows × cols.

Read the old grid row by row, left to right, and write the values into the new grid in that same reading order. This is what a CSS grid does when you change the number of columns: the items keep their order and just wrap differently.

If rows · cols is not equal to m · n the refold is impossible; return the original grid unchanged.

examples.why: The reading order is 1 2 3 4 5 6, cut into rows of two. A transpose would give [[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6]], which is not the same thing.
1 · 3 = 3 cells cannot hold 4 values, so the grid comes back unchanged.
A single column: each value gets its own row, still in reading order.

hints: First decide whether the refold is possible at all. What has to match?
Number every cell by its position in reading order: the cell at (i, j) in an m × n grid is number i·n + j.
Cell number k lands at row ⌊k / cols⌋, column k mod cols in the new grid. Walk k from 0 to m·n − 1.

explain.intuition:
Both grids are just different ways of cutting the same flat list of values into rows. So give every cell its position k in reading order. In the old grid, cell (i, j) is number k = i · n + j. In the new grid, number k sits at row ⌊k / cols⌋, column k mod cols.

That index math is how 2D arrays are stored in memory anyway, and it lets you copy directly without building the flat list. Building the flat list first is also fine and just as fast; it only uses a little extra memory.
steps: If rows · cols !== m · n, return the original grid.
For every k from 0 to m · n − 1: copy grid[⌊k / n⌋][k mod n] into out[⌊k / cols⌋][k mod cols].
pitfalls: Mixing up which width to divide by: the source position uses the old width n, the target uses the new width cols.
Transposing instead of refolding. Values must keep their row-by-row reading order.
Only checking rows ≤ m · n instead of exact equality, which leaves holes or drops values.

solutions.title: Flatten, then cut into rows
solutions.idea: Read all values into one list, then slice that list into pieces of length cols.

solutions.title: Direct index mapping
solutions.idea: Reading-order number k is at (k / n, k % n) in the old grid and at (k / cols, k % cols) in the new one.

followups: Refold column by column instead of row by row. Which formulas change?
Return a view object that reads the old grid through the new shape without copying anything.
